notes: Selection notes: The paper selects 16 late-type candidate HVSs from prior literature and its own ADQL query (T:p2-b7, T:p18-b73). star 1, star 2, star 3, star 4, star 6, star 9, star 10, star 11, star 12, star 13, and star 14 are recorded as follow_up: Table 1's Reference column attributes them to prior candidate-HVS catalogs (T:p5-b0), and the paper's final bound classification (T:p16-b3) does not remove follow_up eligibility. star 5 (Gaia DR3 1396963577886583296) is also prior-catalog follow_up; it is called marginally unbound at 1σ in Section 6.1 (T:p9-b7) but 'marginally bound' in the abstract and Figure 2 caption (T:p1-b10, T:p10-b0; image I:p10-b0), so I did not upgrade it to candidates_found. star 7 (Gaia DR3 1383279090527227264) is candidates_found because the final assessment calls it definitively/very likely unbound (T:p10-b0, T:p16-b3; image I:p10-b0). star 8 (Gaia DR3 1478837543019912064) is candidates_found on the paper's explicit conditional statement that it could be unbound from the escape-velocity overlap (T:p10-b0; image I:p10-b0), although the abstract and summary call the marginal pair bound. Excluded: star 15 (Gaia DR3 3713862039077776256) and star 16 (Gaia DR3 4531308286776328832) were newly selected by the authors' ADQL query as candidate HVSs (T:p5-b0, T:p18-b73) but are part of the final 'remainder ... bound' group (T:p16-b3) and have no prior-literature candidacy, so neither retained candidates_found nor follow_up applies. The contaminant Gaia DR3 4150939038071816320 was in the initial sample but is explicitly rejected as not an extreme velocity star, V_r ~ -21.6 km/s (T:p3-b8). HVS1 and HD 271791 are cited context, not studied targets.

star 1: Table 1 (T:p5-b0 and I:p5-b0) gives star 1's RA, Dec, Bailer-Jones distance, and follow-up RV, but no parallax or proper motions. The paper does not report numerical bound/unbound probabilities for star 1; it only classifies the sample qualitatively. The galactocentric radius and total velocity for star 1 are not tabulated numerically; they are approximate readings from Figure 2 (I:p10-b0, caption T:p10-b0).

star 2: No per-star parallax, proper-motion components, bound/unbound probabilities, or tabulated galactocentric radius/GRF speed are reported for star 2. Figure 2 plots a galactocentric distance and total velocity for the sample, but no numerical values for star 2 are given, so those graphical positions were not extracted as reported quantities.

star 3: The target is identified as star 3 / Gaia DR3 2629296824480015744 in Table 1 (T:p5-b0, I:p5-b0). No explicit scalar values for parallax, proper motions, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame total speed, or bound/unbound probability are reported for this star in the supplied material.

star 4: For star 4 (Gaia DR3 3784964943489710592), no numerical parallax or proper-motion components are tabulated in the supplied text or tables. Figure 2 shows an approximate position/velocity but does not provide exact tabulated values, so those quantities were not extracted.

star 5: No numerical parallax, proper-motion, or bound/unbound probability is reported for star 5 in the supplied material. Section 6.1 (T:p9-b7) calls stars 5 and 8 "marginally unbound (1σ level)", while the Figure 2 caption (T:p10-b0) says star 5 is "marginally bound"; no numerical probability is given. The galactocentric radius and total velocity are only shown graphically in Figure 2 and are therefore approximate readings.

star 6: The galactocentric radius and Galactic-rest-frame total speed for star 6 are not tabulated; the values given are approximate readings from the labeled star 6 point in Figure 2 (I:p10-b0). No individual numerical bound or unbound probability is reported for star 6 in the supplied material.

star 7: Star 7 is Gaia DR3 1383279090527227264. The galactocentric radius and total velocity are displayed only graphically in Figure 2; the values 8.8 kpc and 640 km/s are approximate readings from the labeled point/error bar. The paper describes star 7 as definitively/likely unbound but does not report a numerical bound or unbound probability in the supplied material. No parallax or proper-motion values are tabulated in the supplied text.

star 8: For star 8, the paper gives qualitative kinematic classifications rather than numerical bound/unbound probabilities. Figure 2 (I:p10-b0) plots galactocentric radius and total velocity for star 8, but supplies no tabulated numerical values; the r and v_total entries above are approximate readings from that figure. No individual parallax or proper-motion values are provided in the supplied text.

star 9: Star 9 (Gaia DR3 1552278116525348096) is among the remaining stars described as bound, but no numeric bound/unbound probability is reported. The supplied text does not tabulate parallax, proper motions, galactocentric radius, or Galactic rest-frame total speed for star 9; Figure 2 (I:p10-b0) shows its position/velocity graphically without exact values, so those quantities are omitted.

star 10: The supplied tables do not tabulate parallax, proper motions, galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame total speed, or bound/unbound probabilities for star 10; only the Table 1 quantities above are extracted.

star 11: Star 11 is identified with Gaia DR3 source id 4395399303719163904 in Table 1 (T:p5-b0), which supplies RA, Dec, Bailer-Jones distance, and ground-based radial velocity. The paper refers to star 11 among the remaining stars as apparently bound, but reports no numerical bound/unbound probability for it; no numerical parallax, proper-motion components, galactocentric radius, or Galactic-rest-frame speed is provided for this star in the supplied material.

star 12: Table 1 (T:p5-b0; I:p5-b0) lists RA, Dec, Bailer-Jones et al. (2021) distance, and RV for star 12 = Gaia DR3 1598160152636141568; no parallax or proper-motion components are tabulated in the supplied material. The galactocentric radius and total Galactic-rest-frame velocity are not tabulated; they are approximate graphical readings from Figure 2 (I:p10-b0), where star 12 is labeled near r ≈ 8.6 kpc and v_total ≈ 320 km/s. No numerical bound or unbound probability is reported for star 12; the summary places it among the remaining bound candidates (T:p16-b3).

star 13: Target identified as star 13 / Gaia DR3 4535258625890434944. Table 1 provides the exact equatorial coordinates, Bailer-Jones et al. (2021) distance, and ground-based radial velocity. No parallax, proper-motion components, or individual bound/unbound probabilities are reported for star 13; the paper only states qualitatively that it belongs to the bound remainder. The galactocentric radius and total Galactic-rest-frame speed are not tabulated numerically and are only shown graphically in Figure 2, so their values above are approximate readings from the labeled point. Figure 2 and the surrounding text show some inconsistent "marginally bound" versus "marginally unbound" wording for stars 5 and 8, but this does not affect star 13.

star 14: The paper places star 14 among the high-velocity stars judged bound, but does not report a numerical bound or unbound probability for it (T:p16-b3). The supplied material does not provide a tabulated parallax, proper-motion components, galactocentric radius, or Galactic-rest-frame total speed for star 14; Figure 2 plots its position in the total-speed versus galactocentric-radius plane without stating numerical values in the text (T:p10-b0, I:p10-b0).
